newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER SHOWCASE-TACTICS AND STRATEGY OF BETIS AND REAL MADRID.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-TACTICS AND STRATEGY OF BETIS AND REAL MADRID.

text.p: A look at the strengths and weaknesses of Real Madrid and Real Betis, who meet in the Spanish league in the Santiago Bernabeu stadium on Saturday (kick-off 1930 gmt).
Real Madrid:
Strategy:

Fabio Capello uses a fairly conventional 4-4-2 formation, and has been widely criticised for negative tactics, excessive reliance on counter-attacks, and for introducing a long ball philosophy to a group of skillful players capable of playing better.
However Real have begun to weld together as a unit in the last few games, with Raul Gonzalez taking the helm.

Panucci, Hierro, Alkorta and Roberto Carlos will almost certainly form the defence against Betis. Victor or Amavisca will be on the right side of midfield, together with Redondo, Seedorf and Raul. Raul in particular will move forward to support strikers Suker, on the left, and Mijatovic on the right.
Strengths:

Although he has had some problems in the air in the last four games, goalkeeper Illgner is a tower of strength at the back, while both his substitutes -- Canizares and Paco Buyo -- would stroll into practically any European club side.
Brazilian defender Roberto Carlos moves up well to create danger down the left, while Fernando Hierro is not only the mainstay of the defence but is also strong going forward through the middle.
Both Roberto Carlos -- who blasted an extraordinary left-foot strike past Betis keeper Toni Prats earlier this season -- and the right-footed Hierro are superb set-piece specialists.

The same goes for the the Balkan strike pair of Davor Suker and Predrag Mijatovic, and it is in their individual brilliance, together with that of teenager Raul Gonzalez that Real's true strength lies.
Weaknesses:

Under Capello Real have played effectively but only recently have started to play with much style and are only now gelling as a team. They depend excessively on Mijatovic, Suker and Raul making the best out of half-chances.
The long-ball philosophy, which Capello denies exists, means that at times the midfield seems not to exist at all.
There are problems at the back. Despite signing Illgner because of Capello's insistence on buying a taller keeper, Real have had problems in the air, where Betis' Roberto Rios can be devastating.
Capello has solid performers, but no real match-winners to call upon from the bench, and, with the exception of Emilio Amavisca, is woefully short of capable reserve strikers.
Motivation:

A win would leave Real Madrid 11 points clear, and further pressurise Barcelona coach Bobby Robson in Sunday's game with Racing Santander. It would also almost certainly end Betis' outside hopes of taking the championship.
Probable starting line-up:

Goalkeeper -- Bodo Illgner; Defenders -- Christian Panucci, Fernando Hierro, Rafael Alkorta, Roberto Carlos; Midfielders -- Victor Sanchez, Fernando Redondo, Clarence Seedorf, Raul Gonzalez; Strikers -- Predrag Mijatovic, Davor Suker.
Real Betis:
Strategy:
The criticisms made of Capello of not making enough of his team, could hardly be levelled against Betis coach Lorenzo Serra Ferrer.
In defence and midfield he has taken a number of unsung players, several of them the product of junior sides, and turned them into a compact and efficient unit.
Betis changed strategy at the beginning of the season, and now play with a three-man defence, with Rios on the right, Vidakovic in the middle and Olias on the left.

The five-man midfield allows Jarni and Finidi to move up on the wings to feed balls to front-man Alfonso Perez, who is normally partnered by either Kowalczyk or Pier. Alfonso may be suspended for Saturday's game.
Strengths:
Betis have picked up more than their fair share of lucky breaks this season and seem to have a habit of turning around games with penalties, or after seeing opponents sent off.
Serra Ferrer is a superb organiser and is adaptable, often rearranging his team at half-time.
Betis are the only side to have scored in every game, and are still unbeaten away. Their success is built on a solid defence in which international Roberto Rios is a tower of strength.
Rios comes forward powerfully and plays much the same role as Fernando Hierro does for Real Madrid. Defender Olias has also become an unlikely hero this season with several goals.
In both Finidi and Jarni, Betis have players of true class down the wing, capable of beating opposing players and finding Alfonso -- who has 10 goals this season -- in the middle.
Weaknesses:
Betis' star player is undboutedly former Real Madrid man Alfonso Perez. Betis have appealed against his suspension, but his probable absence means Betis will be without their leading goalscorer.
Without Alfonso, there must be question marks over the strike power offered by Kowalzcyk, Sabas and Pier, particularly against a defence as mean as that of Real Madrid.

Although Betis have pulled results out of the bag away against average teams, they have already slipped up at home to bigger sides such as Barcelona or Deportivo Coruna. They had led in both games, but looked uncharateristically fragile at the back.
Despite the massive mid-season outlay of club owner Lopera, Betis are still short of really quality players, and unlike Real Madrid rarely find themselves sidelining full internationals.
Motivation:
The prospect of coming home as heroic victors from the Santiago Bernabeu stadium is incentive enough for most players.

But in the case of traditional outsiders Betis, a result would virtually guarantee a UEFA Cup place, maintain outside hopes of taking the title and significantly increase the chance of beating Barcelona to Spain's second Champions' League slot -- all of which seemed impossible dreams until recently.
Probable starting line-up:

Goalkeeper -- Toni Prats; Defenders -- Roberto Rios, Hristo Vidakovic, Tomas Olias; Midfielders -- Finidi George, Juan Merino, Juan Canas, Alexis Trujillo, Robert Jarni; Strikers -- Juan Sabas, Pier Cherubino.
